s9.title: 2056 OP Robotics | Behind the Bumpers | FRC 2025 REEFSCAPE

bet.text: Pick up coral in any orientation, to speed up cycles as much as possible. The team says it wanted this from the beginning of the season.

demand.text: The binder requires reach to the net, the processor and every reef level, and a climb that stays up after the buzzer.
The team floor feeds and judged a human player on each side essential.

auto.text: One specific auto scores five pieces. It starts farther away at an angle, so the robot rotates less and scores the first piece faster, and it places after about 40 ms aligned.
Driving is PID to a chain of points. A coral the Limelight sees updates the target point.

cycle.text: Intake, straightenator, cradle, gripper handoff, then hold to auto-align; LEDs turn blue when ready to score.
Hybrid cycles take an algae and a coral together and score both at the back, for two cycles at about the cost of one.

endgame.text: Surgical tubing deploys the climber and a Dyneema winch lifts the robot. A ratchet stops back-driving.
Horns guide the cage in, a protrusion stops it rotating, and a magnet secures it. It works at any cage angle, but the team prefers square.

fallback.text: One button homes the intake, arm and elevator and another purges the intake. The driver can override the chosen left or right branch.

gave_up.text: Algae is held by stalling the gripper motor, which the team says it can do only for a limited time.
A match analyst calls the vertical L1 drop inconsistent in general and credits 2056's stacking to practice, driver skill and arm geometry.
A forum poster puts 2056 10 to 15 points behind two robots, likely from L1 stacking; a reply disputes that, and a later post says only 6 points.

changed.text: To save weight, the arm went from 2 x 2 x 1/8 in tube to formed sheet metal, and the gripper from an X60 at 11.5:1 to an X44 at 19.5:1.
The straightenator went from one motor to one per side, because coral entering parallel to the intake jammed.

outcome.text: 68-7-0 in official play; won the Daly division; captain of the Daly alliance on Einstein; ranked 1 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 137.23, Daly).

solves.text: Stay stable when scoring, with a low center of mass

facts.text: SDS MK4i L2 modules on Kraken X60s, top speed
Chassis 32 in long by 28 in wide in 3 x 1 x 1/8 in tube, with a 1/16 in solid baseplate as shear plate
X44 steering on a shifted adapter plate with a 12 tooth pinion saves nearly 2 lb

solves.text: Acquire coral in any orientation without jamming, and survive high energy impacts

facts.text: Width
A floating top roller, kicker roller and smooth ramp take coral even perpendicular to the intake
Rollers: X60 with a 4:1 belt on a shaft coaxial with the pivot; pivot: X44 at 51:1 through #25 chain
1/4 in polycarbonate held by large aluminum clamping plates; star wheels on a polycarbonate tube at the front
It retracts by itself when a beam break sees a coral

solves.text: Align coral quickly for a repeatable handoff, without jamming

facts.text: One X44 per side at 3:1, with compliant and star wheels
On a current spike the two sides briefly run in opposite directions to unjam and align the coral
It feeds the coral under the elevator into the cradle

cost.text: The first version, with both sides coupled to one motor, jammed on coral that entered parallel to the intake

solves.text: Keep the coral constrained for a repeatable handoff from intake to gripper

facts.text: Two-piece PA-CF print, aligned and glued on dowel pins
A lip stops the coral and a step keeps it from bouncing back
One beam break stops or slows the coral; a second automates the handoff

functions.name: Gripper Arm

solves.text: Hold both game pieces with one mechanism

functions.type: one compliant-wheel gripper on a sheet metal arm

facts.text: Arm of riveted 1/16 in formed sheet metal on a 3/4 in tube, X44 at 59:1
A floating dead axle in slots, with a jack screw, tensions the #25 chain
3 in compliant wheels on an X44 at 19.5:1 pinch algae
When scoring coral the wheels outtake at the velocity of the chassis to release smoothly
A beam break detects algae and automates the coral handoff

cost.text: Algae is held by stalling the motor, for a limited time only

functions.name: Elevator

solves.text: The elevator could limit cycle time, so the aim was to move it as quickly as possible

functions.type: two-stage continuous elevator with internal belt

facts.text: Two X60s at 5:1 on a 30T pulley, 18 mm wide 5 mm HTD belt
Full range of motion in about
SDS bearing blocks, billet corner gussets, knee braces and a 3/8 in U plate against splay
The fixed frame is 2 x 2 tube for lateral stiffness

solves.text: Line up easily, lift the robot off the ground and stay up after the buzzer

facts.text: Surgical tubing deploys it; 1/8 in Dyneema on a 3/4 in spool lifts, X44 at 18:1
A 1/2 in ratchet prevents back-driving
A magnet stops the cage bouncing out, and collars stop it slipping out
Large 3D printed guides eliminate catch points and speed up lining up
Climber weight

solves.text: Never lose sight of the tag while scoring

facts.text: Two Limelight 3Gs track reef tags, and a Limelight 4 with a Hailo accelerator tracks coral
All vision uses 2D tracking; position comes from the vector to the tag, robot heading and tag location
While the intake button is held and a coral is seen, the chassis shifts to line up with it, in proportion to its speed
Limelights on both elevator uprights keep a tag in sight while aligning

solves.text: Tell the driver when the robot is ready to score

facts.text: LEDs go from red to blue and the controller rumbles when position and elevator errors are small enough to score
White means a coral is acquired and green an algae

functions.name: Weight Reduction

solves.text: Fit 150 lb of robot into a 115 lb box without losing stiffness or scoring function

functions.type: pocketing, formed sheet and lighter parts

facts.text: X44s where possible, for 1/2 lb less per motor
Hollow shafts, pocketed ribs, printed gears and pulleys, tapped plates in place of nuts, nylon and aluminum bolts
Sponsor panel and coral covers were counted as bumper weight

decisions.choice: One mechanism for both game pieces
decisions.because: the team did not want to over complicate the robot
coral can slip independently, which makes jamming much less likely
the team saw early how much the elevator could limit cycles
it balances speed and acceleration for the game's short cycles

decisions.choice: Gripper motor mounted away from the gripper
decisions.because: it protects the motor and reduces the moment on the pivot
strings of points are simple to write and easy to adapt

decisions.choice: No tracking of where pieces were scored
decisions.because: a piece that is knocked off then needs no update
decisions.cost: the driver has to keep eyes up

decisions.choice: One driver and two human players
decisions.because: the robot floor feeds, so a human player on each side felt essential
decisions.cost: every function has to fit on one controller
